# Draft: refund agent, note to the steering group

For Dana Okafor, written 23 November 2026. Draft only. Nothing has been sent.

## For you first

AI BVF returned Fix for the customer service agent. An agent answered these questions from evidence it quoted. No person has confirmed the answers.

The gap sits with you. The steering minutes of 12 November say: "Action: Dana to propose an owner for the limits by January."

The same minutes say: "Pilot from 1 December with the returns team." The note below makes your proposal. The name and the dates are blank for you to fill.

## The note

- To: Mira Aalto, Piet Hauer, Sam Lind
- From: Dana Okafor
- Subject: Refund agent: written limits and a named owner

All,

The minutes of 12 November record three things on the refund agent.

- "Refund limits to be agreed after the pilot and written into the service policy then."
- "Nobody is named yet to approve refunds above the limit or to switch the agent off."
- "Action: Dana to propose an owner for the limits by January."

Here is my proposal.

1. We write down what the agent may do without approval. It goes into the service policy by [date].
2. [Name] approves anything above that.
3. The same person has the right to stop the agent.

The pilot starts on 1 December. I want these three points settled by [date].

Send me any objection by [date].

Dana

## What AI BVF returned

- Verdict: Fix
- Summary: "Fix one thing first. The question on how the work changes comes after that."
- Holding it back: Risk and control
  - Question: "What can the agent do without a person approving it, and who can stop it?"
  - Answer: "It works within limits, and nobody has written them down or owns them."
  - Quote: "The agent will work within a refund limit of 50 euros per order. Refund limits to be agreed after the pilot and written into the service policy then. Nobody is named yet to approve refunds above the limit or to switch the agent off." (steering group minutes, 12 November 2026, item 1)
  - Needed: "Its limits are written down, and a named person approves anything above them and can stop it."
- First step: "Write down what the agent may do without approval, name the person who approves anything above that, and give that person the right to stop it."
- The three answers that do not hold it back:
  - "What does it cost to build and run, and what does it return each year?" Answer: "The return covers the cost, on figures finance has checked." Quote: "Cost: 96,000 euros a year for licences and integration." "Return: 180,000 euros a year from fewer first-line contacts handled by people." "Finance has checked both figures against last year's contact volumes and signed them off on 3 November. Neither figure has been measured in a pilot yet." (business case, version 3, 4 November 2026)
  - "Which business result does this move, and by how much?" Answer: "A result the organisation already tracks, with a target and a named executive owner." Quote: "First response under two minutes for 80 percent of contacts, measured monthly on the service dashboard." "Owner: Dana Okafor, Customer Director." "The refund agent is the main lever for this objective." (Customer objectives 2027, Objective 2, undated)
  - "Who owns the change, and are the time and budget for it funded?" Answer: "An owner is named and the change work is funded." Quote: "Project lead: Sam Lind, full time on this until April." "Budget for the change work: 40,000 euros, for training and new team guides. Approved by Dana Okafor." (project plan, 6 November 2026)
- Not asked yet: "What has been redesigned in the work itself before go-live?" The process design of 10 November is on file for it. It covers the workflow, the roles and the override rights. On measures it says: "The team's measures stay as they are for now. Handling time per contact remains the main target."
- Who answered: "An agent answered these questions from evidence it quoted. No person has confirmed the answers."
